correctness.rationale: Derivatives Z^q,X^q,Y^q show smoothness. Exact expansion on the tangent shows contact >=q; the explicitly calculated residual point R=σΦ² lies on the tangent and the curve, so Bézout yields q[P]+[R(P)]. Fixed locus is reduced and lies in Fq6 because R³=Φ^6. Hilbert 90 gives representatives [a:a^{q4}:a^{q2}] modulo Fq2*, with curve condition Trace_{q3/q}(Norm_{q6/q3}(a))=0 and exactly q³+1 classes. Degree-one and degree-two fixed loci reduce to σ eigenlines, with h_q cases; degree-three fixed points correspond to a twisted Fq-projective plane with Tr(a²)=0, giving q+1 points (smooth conic for odd q, line for even q). Subtracting yields geometric exact-degree counts h_q,0,q+1-h_q,q³-q. The accompanying exact finite-field executable fully enumerates and checks q=2,3,4,5; the general claim rests on the mathematical proof rather than experimental extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Nearest concrete primary coverage is Oyono–Ritzenthaler (arXiv:1006.0873, Section 2): the characteristic-three Klein quartic is isomorphic to the Fermat quartic and has 28 hyperflexes, so that specialization is excluded from the novel contribution. Arakelian–Borges (arXiv:1409.8549) is full-text relevant background on nonclassical tangency but treats a family of power-substitution Fermat-type curves rather than the present cyclic monomials, with no identified fixed residual tangent map or Frobenius degree distribution. Relevant published mathematical records and prior accessible ledger claims were searched and compared by implication; no direct stronger or equivalent statement was located. The assessed addition is the uniform norm–trace classification in arbitrary q, especially q>=4, including exact degree one/three/six points and the finite-scheme zeta function. An unlocated specialized source could still cover this and remains a serious priority risk.
residual_risks: Highly specialized finite-geometric literature on nonclassical cyclic Klein curves or tangential correspondences could already imply the uniform result; a non-hit in electronic searches is not uniqueness proof.
The q=3 case is fully covered by the 2010 primary paper (and earlier tradition), and is used only for calibration.
A publication that counts totally tangent points through a dual-curve invariant rather than the norm-trace notation could dominate the result without matching search wording.

value.rationale: The geometric locus where the tangent has the full Bézout contact q+1 is canonical and motivated by the exceptional inflection behavior of cyclic nonclassical plane curves. Uniform q³+1 cardinality, degree ≤6, a complete arithmetic closed-point count and its zeta factorization quantify a natural finite geometric subscheme and distinguish higher q cases from the historically known Klein quartic; this is not arbitrary numerical slicing or unmotivated table completion.
